---
title: "Dynamic Batching"
description: "The grouping of incoming requests into batches at runtime to improve processing efficiency."
term: "Dynamic Batching"
letter: "D"
category: "Inference Systems"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

Dynamic batching groups requests that arrive around the same time and
processes them together. It can improve hardware utilization for model
inference without requiring clients to submit a batch themselves.

## Technical explanation

An inference server collects compatible requests until a maximum batch
size, timeout, or scheduling condition is reached. The resulting batch
is sent through the model, and outputs are separated and returned to the
corresponding requests. Batching policy must balance throughput, queueing
latency, memory, and request compatibility.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Many accelerators process larger batches more efficiently, so dynamic
batching can increase throughput and lower per-request compute cost.
However, waiting to form batches can increase response latency and may
be inappropriate for strict real-time workloads.

## How it works

The serving layer queues requests, groups those with compatible inputs,
executes a model call for the group, and maps each result back to its
request. Configuration may limit batch size and the time a request waits.

## Practical example

A text-embedding service can briefly queue several independent requests,
encode them in one model call, and return each embedding to its caller.

## Common misconceptions

- Dynamic batching does not combine unrelated requests into one semantic
  prompt; it batches computation while keeping request outputs separate.
- Larger batches do not always improve end-to-end latency.
- Batches may be constrained by input shapes, model features, or response
  requirements.
